main_text.l: feruare maximè oportet: qui grato animo
aliorum agnoscere adhortationes debèt.
Sumendæ igitur hîc sententiæ erunt ex tri-
bus locis: caufis, adiunctis, effectis: & o-
stendendum: pondus apud nos magnum
exhortationem amici habuiffe: effeciffe
illud: vt nihil in votis habeamus magis,
quàm eidem fatis nos facere poffe. Propo-
fita habere illam cómoda, & multa, & ma-
gna: laudem, honorem, opes, &c. effe ho-
neftam quoq;, æquam, iuftam: prudentiæ
& fidei plenam. Tum coluiffe nos & ob-
feruaffe ab ineunte ætate amicum: pro-
pter paternam necefsitudinem, amorem
noftri fingularem: prudentiam, autorita-
tem, promerita deniq; & plurima & ma-
xima: ideoq; neq; iam fine reprehenfione
graui ab eius nos difcrepare monitis pof-
e. Motus hîc duo locum habent: αἰχύνη[?]
παθητικὰ[?] ἀρ pudor feu verecundia, & ἐλπὶς[?] fpes, quę ex
citatur ... cùm fcilicet promittimus
nosstudiosè diligenterq; facturos ea, quæ
à nobis amicus requirit. Conciliantes ve- rò
fententiæ funt, quę laudem & commen
dationem, gratiarum actionem, grati ani-
mi pollicitationem, petitionem habent.
Fauemus enim iis, qui adhortationibus
locum relinquunt: qui earúdem & fidem,

page.notes: The Greek words in the text and margin (αἰχύνη, παθητικὰ, ἐλπὶς, ἀρ, ἰδ̀ἀ) are only partly legible on the scan and are marked [?]. The printed margin reads "ἀρ" and "gumenta" as a word split across lines ("argumenta"); the first margin note sequence is read as printed. The "citatur" line has a Greek word (ζωγράφος-like form, printed "ζωγρίσε") and an ellipsis-like gap that is not transcribed as text. A small stray mark under the text on the page centre is not printed text and is omitted. The margin note "Sententiæ rè" is read with uncertainty.
